sections.html:
Delaware County is in east central Indiana, with Muncie as both the county seat and the largest city, about 50 miles northeast of Indianapolis. The 2020 census counted 111,903 people in the county, and 65,194 in Muncie. Many houses here are older, so roofs, gutters and furnaces get close attention in an inspection.

The economy has shifted from manufacturing toward education, health care and retail, with Ball State University and IU Health Ball Memorial Hospital among the largest employers. Growth has concentrated on the north side of Muncie, while the older industrial south side has seen less. Muncie spreads across Center, Hamilton, Harrison, Liberty and Mount Pleasant townships, and the county Assessor's Office keeps property cards with some transfer history.

sections.h2: Due dates and where to pay
sections.html:
Delaware County property taxes are due on or before May 10 and November 10, and the date moves to the next business day if it lands on a weekend or holiday.

The Auditor's office is at 100 West Main Street, Room 103, Muncie, IN 47305, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The phone number is 765-747-7717. The Treasurer is at 100 W Main St, Room 102.

  • To change the mailing address on your tax statement, go to the Auditor's office.
  • If statements are not coming in your name, contact the Plat Room at the same number.
  • Mortgage deductions need signatures, so visit the Auditor in person. A reverse mortgage can qualify with a lender statement showing the debt.

Late payment brings a penalty of 5% of the delinquent tax when paid within 30 days and no earlier delinquency exists, or 10% in other cases.

Indiana's Form 130 deadline is June 15 of the year the county mails the assessment notice, or of the year the tax bill goes out when no notice is sent. You file one petition for each parcel with the assessing official.

The assessor then holds an informal meeting and reports back to the Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals. The hearing must happen within 180 days of filing, with notice mailed at least 30 days ahead. If you disagree with the result, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Good evidence includes a recent appraisal, sales of similar nearby houses, and photos or estimates for repairs. Check the property card at the Assessor's office first, because a wrong square footage or a structure that no longer exists is the simplest error to correct.

A homestead deduction can matter as much to a final bill as a lower assessed value. The standard deduction has been 60% of assessed value up to $48,000, with a January 5 filing date. The rule was amended effective January 1, 2025, so confirm the current figures with the Auditor.

If you are selling, remember that the buyer has to claim the deduction in their own name. A house that was your homestead may go back to a higher tax class if the new owner rents it out or leaves it empty, so do not assume your bill carries over.

When a Delaware County property is sold at a tax sale, only the owner whose property was sold can claim the surplus. Anyone else, even with a power of attorney, must petition the court.

The surplus becomes available only after the court issues a tax deed and the deed is recorded with the Delaware County Recorder's Office. Questions go to the Auditor's office at 765-747-7717.

Selling the house before a tax sale can avoid losing it to a certificate holder, and it keeps the extra costs from piling up.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or other issues
sections.html:
Delaware County sellers often have older houses, inherited property or rental units. The sales disclosure form is required before a deed reaches the auditor, and each parcel needs its own form.

  • Get a payoff figure for taxes and any penalties.
  • Confirm the mailing address on the tax bill.
  • Gather estate papers if the owner has died.
  • Decide whether repairs make sense before selling.

Cash buyers can close without a lender appraisal, and the title company settles taxes from your proceeds.

A practical order: confirm the balance at the Auditor's office, make sure the address on the bill is current so statements reach you, and tell the title company early if there is a reverse mortgage or any other lien on the property. For rental units, remember each parcel needs its own sales disclosure form, so a seller with several parcels should list them all with the closing agent at the start.

If the owner has died, bring the estate papers and the deed history. The Assessor's property card shows some transfer history, which helps a title company see whether the names line up before the sale record is filed.

faqs.q: When are Delaware County property taxes due?
faqs.a: On or before May 10 and November 10 each year, and the date shifts when it falls on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: Where do I change the mailing address on my Delaware County tax bill?
faqs.a: Make the request at the Auditor's office, 100 West Main Street, Room 103, Muncie. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and the phone is 765-747-7717.

faqs.q: Who can claim surplus from a Delaware County tax sale?
faqs.a: Only the owner whose property was sold. Anyone else must petition the court, even with a power of attorney. Surplus is available after a tax deed is issued and recorded.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Delaware County assessment?
faqs.a: June 15 of the year the notice or tax bill is mailed, on Form 130. File one petition per parcel and check your notice for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Delaware County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid taxes and penalties are paid from your proceeds at closing, and a cash sale can close before a tax sale happens.
